points: At the banquet of wine the king again asked Esther her petition, promising it would be granted even to the half of the kingdom.

note.label: Esther 7: Haman Hanged on His Own Gallows

points: Esther pleaded for her life and the life of her people, for they had been sold to be destroyed, slain, and to perish, and had it been only bondage she would have held her tongue.

note.label: Esther 7: Haman Hanged on His Own Gallows

points: The king demanded to know who he was that dared presume in his heart to do such a thing.

note.label: Esther 7: Haman Hanged on His Own Gallows

points: Esther named the adversary and enemy as this wicked Haman, and Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.
Sitting at the table, Haman could hardly eat, for he had just arrayed Mordecai and just heard his own household warn him he would fall before the Jews, and now he was exposed at the dinner table.

note.label: Esther 7: Haman Hanged on His Own Gallows

points: The king rose in his wrath and went into the palace garden, and Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther, seeing that evil was determined against him.

note.label: Esther 7: Haman Hanged on His Own Gallows

points: When the king returned, Haman had fallen upon the bed where Esther was, and the king took it as an assault on the queen in his own house.
As the word went out of the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.

note.label: Esther 7: Haman Hanged on His Own Gallows

points: Harbonah, a chamberlain, told the king of the gallows fifty cubits high that Haman had made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standing at Haman's house.

note.label: Esther 7: Haman Hanged on His Own Gallows

points: The king commanded Haman be hanged on it, and they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai, and the king's wrath was pacified. This is the Most High, a man of war, and this is how He moves.
